title: Capital-gains reinvestment (rollover) exemptions FY 2026-27 - Section 54 (residential house to residential house), 54F (any long-term asset other than a house to a residential house) and 54EC (a house-gain reinvested in notified infrastructure bonds, capped at Rs 50,00,000): the proportional rule (exemption = the smaller of the net gain and the amount actually reinvested in time), the statutory time windows (54EC within 6 months; 54 purchase within 1 yr before / 2 yr after sale or construction within 3 yr; 54F within 2 yr), the two exemption-breakers (a missed window and a non-long-term gain), the Capital Gains Account Scheme (CGAS) to hold unspent consideration, the Rs 10 Cr new-asset-cost cap on 54/54F (from AY 2024-25), the post-Finance (No.2) Act 2024 12.5% no-indexation LTCG base, and NRI eligibility (the rollover also reduces the 195 TDS)
publisher: CBDT Budget-2024 capital-gains FAQs (PIB, 24 Jul 2024) / TaxClue 54EC + 54F guides
claims: The post-2024 capital-gains rationalisation: holding periods simplified to 1 year (listed) and 2 years (other assets); LTCG on all assets at 12.5% without indexation; the 112A equity exemption raised to Rs 1.25L; reinvestment (rollover) benefits unchanged in structure

Section 54: a long-term gain on a residential house is exempt to the extent it is reinvested in another residential house - purchase within 1 year before or 2 years after the sale, or construction within 3 years of the sale
Section 54F: a long-term gain on any asset OTHER than a house is exempt to the extent the net consideration is invested in one residential house within 2 years of the sale

Section 54EC: a long-term gain on a house may instead be reinvested in notified infrastructure bonds (NHAI / REC / PFC / IRFC etc.), capped at Rs 50,00,000, within 6 months of the sale; the bond must be held (not sold or converted to money) for the statutory period
The exemption is proportional: it is the SMALLER of the net gain and the amount actually reinvested; reinvesting less than the gain leaves the balance taxable
Two conditions break the exemption: the reinvestment must be inside the statutory window, and the gain must be a LONG-TERM gain

Unspent sale consideration can be parked in a Capital Gains Account Scheme (CGAS) deposit; the exemption holds only if it is deployed within the remaining time, else the uninvested part becomes taxable in the year the deadline lapses

From AY 2024-25 the 54/54F exemption for a single individual/HUF is capped at a new-asset cost of Rs 10 crore; the routes are available to residents and NRIs, and using them also reduces the Section 195 TDS an NRI property buyer withholds
notes: The 54EC notified-bond list is updated by the government each quarter - confirm the open tranche and its investment dates before relying on the 6-month window. The 12.5% no-indexation base and the holding periods are the Finance (No.2) Act 2024 position; re-verify at each Finance Act. The rollover math (exemption = min(gain, reinvested), 54EC 50L cap) is what the rolloverExemption() function models.

title: International Mutual Fund Taxation in India: the AY 2026-27 Section 50AA debt-test and the 12.5% LTCG (no pool) that now reaches non-specified international FoFs and GIFT City schemes
publisher: Foliyo / Sachin Kabra (ex-Director HDFC Private Wealth)
claims: AY 2026-27: a 'Specified Mutual Fund' (Sec 50AA, renumbered Sec 76 in the Income-tax Act 2025) is now a DEBT-based test — a fund that invests >65% of proceeds in debt/money-market instruments (or >=65% in such a fund), measured on the annual average of daily closing figures; it no longer means 'every fund that lacks the domestic-equity threshold'

An international equity FoF or India-listed int'l equity ETF is NOT automatically a Specified MF just because it owns no Indian equity; if it fails the debt test, its units can become long-term after 24 months (unlisted) or 12 months (listed)

Gains on units that DO meet the Sec 50AA specified-fund definition are deemed SHORT-TERM and taxed at the slab rate regardless of holding period
Income-tax Act 2025 section mapping: 111A->196, 112->197, 112A->198, 50AA->76 (effective 1 Apr 2026; the 1961 numbers are still used informally)

title: US stocks taxed in India 2026: the 25% individual dividend withholding (W-8BEN) vs the 30% backup (and the 15% corporate-with-voting-stock figure that is NOT the individual rate), the 24-month / 12.5% no-pool foreign-security CG treatment, the Form 67 FTC cap, Schedule FA no-threshold disclosure, and the FAST-DS 2026 small-taxpayer scheme (Finance Act 2026 Ch. IV, ~15 Aug to 31 Dec 2026)
publisher: Vedanta / WINvesta / Vested / Filewise / Upstox 2026 investor guides + KPMG / CBDT / NDTV FAST-DS 2026 coverage + Income-tax Act 2025 renumbered text
claims: A US dividend paid to an individual Indian resident is subject to 25% US withholding when a Form W-8BEN is on file (the individual US-India treaty rate); without a W-8BEN the 30% backup rate applies; the widely-quoted 15% figure is the corporate-holder-with-substantial-voting-stock treaty rate, NOT the individual rate (cambridgewealth / winvesta)

The dividend is also taxable in India (worldwide income) at the slab rate; the 25% US withholding is credited via Form 67 / Schedule FSI, capped at the lesser of the India dividend tax and the US tax actually paid

US shares are unlisted foreign securities: LTCG after 24 months at 12.5% without indexation and with NO Rs 1.25L pool (the 112A pool is Indian-listed-equity only); STCG (<=24 months) at the slab rate (vested / winvesta / filewise / upstox)
Schedule FA disclosure of a US brokerage position is mandatory every year while held, with no minimum threshold; foreign-source income (dividends / CG) is reported in Schedule FSI
The LRS investment remittance that funds the US purchase attracts 20% TCS above the Rs 10L aggregate threshold (recoverable at ITR); education / medical / tour TCS is 2% from 1 Apr 2026

FAST-DS 2026 = Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers - Disclosure Scheme 2026, Finance Act 2026 Chapter IV (sections 130-144), a one-time window ~15 Aug to 31 Dec 2026; Category A = undisclosed foreign assets/income up to Rs 1 cr (a specified tax + an equal additional amount), Category B = up to Rs 5 cr for assets from disclosed income / non-resident period (a flat Rs 1L fee with immunity); it is the amnesty layer for UNDISCLOSED assets, distinct from a normal Schedule FA filing (KPMG flash news + CBDT FAQs + NDTV Profit / NationPath)
limitations: The 25% individual dividend-withholding figure is the current US-India treaty position per the cited 2026 guides and can move with a treaty renewal or an IRS change; confirm the specific W-8BEN validity for the withholding year. The FAST-DS window dates (15 Aug to 31 Dec 2026) are the notified dates and the scheme is one-time - it cannot be reused. The Rs 10L LRS TCS threshold is the post-Finance-Act-2025 figure. All figures are planning inputs; reconcile with Form 67 / Schedule FSI / the ITR e-file and a CA before acting.

title: FAST-DS 2026 valuation + due-diligence layer: the Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers-Disclosure Scheme Rules, 2026 (G.S.R. 732(E) dated 14 Aug 2026, in force 16 Aug 2026, last date 31 Dec 2026) - the 31 Mar 2026 valuation date (Rule 2(1)(e)), the Rule 3 per-asset-class FMV methods + RBI-reference-rate currency conversion (Rule 3(4)/(5)), the 20% valuation-variance safeguard (Rule 5(2)), the four-form chain (Forms 1-2-3-4, Rules 5-8) + the 1%/month late-payment interest (Rule 7), and the limited immunity that does NOT settle FEMA exposure
publisher: CA R N Mohil (TaxGuru, 18 Aug 2026) + the CBDT FAST-DS 2026 official FAQs (13 Aug 2026) + the notified G.S.R. 732(E) Rules + EY 2026 technical alert
claims: The FAST-DS 2026 Rules were notified vide G.S.R. 732(E) dated 14 Aug 2026, came into force 16 Aug 2026, and prescribe 31 Dec 2026 as the "last date" (Rule 2(4)); the valuation date is fixed at 31 Mar 2026 (Rule 2(1)(e)) - not adjustable

Track A (undisclosed foreign asset/income, aggregate up to Rs 1 cr): 30% tax plus an additional amount equal to 100% of that tax = 60% of value; Rule 4 illustrates a Rs 60L bank account + Rs 20L undisclosed income (aggregate Rs 80L within the ceiling) -> tax Rs 24L + additional Rs 24L = Rs 48L

Track B (a specified foreign asset up to Rs 5 cr that was acquired from income accrued abroad while non-resident, or from income already offered to tax but omitted from the return schedule): a flat Rs 1,00,000 fee; Rule 4 illustrates a Rs 3 cr foreign property acquired while non-resident -> Rs 1 lakh

Rule 3 prescribes asset-specific valuation as on 31 Mar 2026: bullion/jewellery/precious stones (3(1)(a)), artistic works (3(1)(b)), quoted shares/securities (3(1)(c)(i)), unquoted equity shares (3(1)(c)(ii)), other unquoted shares/securities (3(1)(c)(iii)), immovable property (3(1)(d)), foreign bank accounts (3(1)(e) - the sum of deposits from opening to 31 Mar 2026 with treatment for redeposits), partnership/AOP/LLP interests (3(1)(f)), and other assets (3(1)(g)); Rule 3(2)/(3) cover assets transferred before the valuation date and assets acquired from proceeds; where valuation is not carried out, the indexed cost of acquisition is deemed to be the FMV

Currency conversion (Rule 3(4)/(5)): an asset in a permitted currency is converted to INR at the RBI reference rate on the valuation date; other currencies convert two-stage through USD using the prescribed foreign-country rate + the RBI reference rate

The four-form electronic process (Rules 5-8): Form 1 (declaration, Rule 5 - separately captures the Track A and Track B computations with annexures), Form 2 (order/determination, Rule 6 - issued by the Principal DGIT or DGIT (Systems)), Form 3 (payment intimation, Rule 7 - payment within 2 months of receipt of Form 2; 1% interest per month or part for delayed payment; part payments recognised), and Form 4 (final certification, Rule 8 - certifying the declaration is valid for Section 139 and conferring the prescribed immunity)

Rule 5(2) valuation-variance safeguard: the declaration is not treated as invalid merely because the FMV declared in Form 1 differs from the value later determined by the assessing officer, provided the variance does not exceed 20% of the declared FMV; above 20% the charge re-computes on the (higher) determined FMV

FAST-DS is taxpayer-specific (companies/LLPs/firms/trusts cannot use it for their employees) and its immunity is LIMITED: it regularises the tax / Black Money Act exposure but does NOT automatically settle FEMA / exchange-control exposure, and does not replace the ongoing Schedule FA obligation
limitations: The 20% valuation-variance safeguard, the per-asset-class Rule 3 methods, and the RBI-reference-rate currency conversion are the operative 2026 positions and can move with a later notification / Budget. The "determined FMV" is what an assessing officer arrives at - the calculator takes it as an input, not a live valuation. Confirm the specific asset class and currency against the notified Rules and a CA before filing Form 1. This is a due-diligence/valuation planning layer, not a Form 1 filing computation.

title: FEMA 1999 exchange-control exposure: the Section 13(1) "up to 3x the sum involved" penalty (vs the FERA-era 9x that does not apply), the Section 15 compounding route via PRAVAAH (up to a Rs 5 cr contravention, the 2025 amendment capping certain compounding fees at Rs 2,00,000, and the non-compoundable Section 3(a) hawala exception), and the LRS USD 250k / NRO USD 1M / ODI individual limits that define the breaching "sum"
publisher: Beacon Filing / VirtualAuditor / APTaxLaw / KS&A 2026 FEMA penalty + compounding coverage + the RBI Master Direction on Compounding of Contraventions under FEMA, 1999 (April 2025 update) + Oquilia Research (NRO USD 1M / LRS USD 250k) + RBI LRS FAQ
claims: FEMA Section 13(1) levies a monetary penalty of up to THREE times the sum involved in the contravention (the current cap; the '9 times' figure was the FERA-era number and does not apply under FEMA 1999)

FEMA Section 15 allows compounding (voluntary settlement) of a compoundable contravention by paying a fee to the RBI (up to a Rs 5 cr contravention) or the Enforcement Directorate (above Rs 5 cr), filed via the PRAVAAH portal; a Section 3(a) hawala offence is NOT compoundable
A 2025 amendment to the FEMA compounding regime caps the fee for certain compounded contraventions at Rs 2,00,000; the applicable fee is set by the RBI per contravention, not a flat tariff

The 'sum involved' in a Section 13 penalty is the breaching remittance, not the asset value: a resident LRS remittance (up to USD 250,000/FY, NRIs excluded), an NRO repatriation (up to USD 1,000,000/FY after Indian tax + Forms 15CA/15CB), or an ODI (individual equity-only, within the LRS limit; individuals cannot provide loans/guarantees)

Tax regularisation (FAST-DS / Schedule FA) and exchange-control regularisation (FEMA compounding) are separate exercises administered by different authorities - the income-tax department vs the RBI / ED - and settling one does not close the other
limitations: The 3x Section 13(1) penalty is a cap ("up to 3x"), the actual adjudicated penalty is case-specific, and the Section 15 compounding fee is set by the RBI per contravention (the Rs 2L is a 2025 cap for a class of contraventions, not a flat price). Confirm the specific contravention's compoundability and fee with the PRAVAAH process / a FEMA practitioner before acting. The LRS / NRO / ODI limits are the 2026 positions and can move with an RBI Master Direction.

title: ODI (Overseas Direct Investment) route 2026: the 26 May 2026 amendment raising the entity automatic-route limit from 300% to 400% of net worth, the USD 1B-per-FY prior-approval trigger, the resident-individual LRS USD 250k/FY equity-only ODI limit, the ODI-vs-OPI definition (unlisted equity / 10%+ listed / control vs a listed under-10% no-control OPI position), and the Form FC-ODI post-fact filing + ~Rs 7,500 late-submission fee
publisher: KAMRIT 26 May 2026 omnibus-route update + Resolut Partners / E-Tax Prime / Beacon Filing 2026 ODI coverage + Khaitan & Co + the RBI OI Rules 2022 ODI/OPI definition + the RBI LRS FAQ

A financial commitment above USD 1 billion in a financial year moves to the prior-RBI-approval route, even within the 400% limit (Master Direction on ODI para 5)

Confirm the operative multiple and fee against the current OI Rules 2022 + Master Direction on ODI before remitting.
